MMOs haven't ceased to be successful. They're just not seen as the fast road to perpetual riches like they once were. The novelty is gone, the buzz has died down, and people have realized that having to rely on the collaboration of internet people in order to fully explore the game's content typically sucks.

When World of Warcraft first came out, old school MMORPG players liked to look down their nose at it for allowing players to solo their way to the level cap and gasp enjoy it. "Why would you play an MMO if you don't want to play with other people?" they would say. "Because it beats playing with assholes like you," is what the response should have been, but people actually tried to explain why they would be enthusiastic about playing a game populated by all kinds of different people without wanting to feel like they had to rely on those people to have fun.

Of course, we know now that an MMO without a robust solo component is not going to do as well as it could, and for all the people who like to write multi-page bullet-point dissertations on why WoW was a bad game and made the industry worse, Blizzard ended up with a couple hundred billion reasons to say, "neener neener."

Nevertheless, there has to also be group content, and that group content has to offer experiences that aren't available in the solo content, so the people who haven't go the patience for elitist jerks ( people who play very well and treat others badly for not playing well), wanna-be elitist jerks (players who only think they play well, but still treat other people badly because it makes their e-peen bigger), noobs (people who would play well if they knew what playing well required, typically prey for elitist jerks and viciously harassed by wanna-be elitist jerks) and scrubs (people who play poorly, have no interest in making an equal contribution, and generally act as though it's their god-given right to be carried to rewards they couldn't earn if everyone in their group played as badly as they did.) And then, of course, are the assholes...part wanna-be elitist jerk, part scrub, all flapping anus.

Of course, by the time you get past the elitist jerks, the wanna-be elitist jerks, the noobs, the scrubs, and the assholes, every once in a while you come across a genuinely decent human being. It's just the people get tired of the 10:1 ratio after a while.

Will MMOs continue to be successful? Yes. But MMORPGs are one of the genres that needs to evolve the most in order to remain viable. New technology and innovation is necessary to make sure that people are logging in and having fun without feeling like they're being left out or left behind because they need too much from other players in order to access the content.

I think that until recently MMOs have been locked into the World of Warcraft formula. Not because that was the only way to make an MMO, but because WoW was making so much fucking money, all with a staff of about 50 guys. So companies saw "10 million subscribers at $15 a month, on 50 full-time employees" and that was what they all wanted. They were so focused on hitting the mark that they didn't stop to think about whether or not the mark was in the right place.

Now that developers are starting to see that even WoW fans are getting bored with WoW, I think there's the potential for successful MMOs again.
